findings.title: Outer loop stays in spawn order, so neighbor reads still don't coalesce across a warp
findings.description:
For a warp to coalesce, neighbouring threads must read neighbouring addresses in the same instruction. The force kernel gives one thread to each original-order agent `i` (`quadrants_fused_kernels.py:355`). Agents `i` and `i+1` are next to each other in spawn order, not in space, so they scan different cells: thread `i` reads `_px_c[start_i + t]` while thread `i+1` reads `_px_c[start_{i+1} + t]`, in unrelated cells. The design keeps this loop (lines 124, 322) and rejects walking the outer loop in coherent order (line 165). That rejected option is the Hoetzlein/FRNN approach the design cites at line 21.

What a coherent layout still gives under the chosen design is per-thread cache-line reuse. That is a real gain, but it is not the "standard ~2–3× DRAM bandwidth improvement" from coalescing that the plan and gate assume (lines 17, 21, 130, 133, 286).

Two supporting claims are also wrong:
- Line 165 says scattered writebacks would be "just as bad as the original gather problem". That is 4 writes per agent against about 1400 reads per agent.
- Line 169 says "adjacent agents' heaps tend to evict slots from the same nearby cell range". Adjacent `i` values are not spatially near each other.

The design needs to either walk the outer loop in coherent slots (accepting a 4-scalar scatter on writeback, or adding a reorder pass), or rewrite its expected-gain reasoning and gate on per-thread locality only.

findings.title: Departs from the plan entry: gate changed, `k_first` removed, FRNN deferred, `radius_only` added
findings.description:
The plan entry (`140-slices.simulation-scaling.md:56`) sets these exit criteria: "k-nearest TPS at N=200k within 20% of **k-first** TPS … no regression on k-first path". It also assigns "k-nearest via FRNN (collect all within radius R, then partial-sort …)" to this slice.

The design instead:
- deletes `k_first`, so the "no regression on k-first path" criterion can't be checked (lines 34, 67, 177-179)
- re-bases the gate on a new `radius_only` mode (line 358)
- defers FRNN to a future slice (lines 75, 187-193)
- adds a third mode-set change that isn't in the plan

Deferring scope the plan assigns is a CONCERN under the review rules. Either update the plan entry to match (gate, modes, FRNN deferral) or bring the design back in line with the plan.

findings.title: Rewritten `k_nearest` loop reads `_px_c[-1]` for uncapped profiles
findings.description:
Today a profile with `max_neighbors` set to `None` is stored as `0` (`agent_state.py:390`), and the current `k_nearest` branch handles it with an explicit uncapped sub-branch (`quadrants_fused_kernels.py:470-486`). Line 68 promotes that sub-branch to `radius_only`, and the AFTER pseudocode drops it from `k_nearest`.

With `max_neighbors=0`:
1. `heap_size < max_neighbors` is false.
2. `dsq < heap_dsq[0]` (the initial value is 1e38) is true.
3. So `evicted = heap_idx[0] = -1`, and the code reads `_px_c[-1]` and de-accumulates garbage.

`heap_push` then refuses to insert (`heap_size > 0` is false), yet the incoming neighbor is still accumulated. The design should keep the uncapped sub-branch in `k_nearest`, or define `k_nearest` with `max_neighbors<=0` as an error.

findings.title: Heap declaration gated by a plain `if` goes out of scope
findings.description:
Line 317 says the `qd.Vector` heap initializer is "gated on `neighbor_mode != NEIGHBOR_MODE_RADIUS_ONLY`". In Taichi/Quadrants, a variable declared inside a non-`qd.static` `if` belongs to that block. The `k_nearest` branch and the pruning block (`quadrants_fused_kernels.py:420`), which use `heap_dsq`/`heap_idx`, are in separate blocks, so the kernel won't compile as described.

The gate needs `if qd.static(neighbor_mode != …)`, and the mode-dispatch `if`s should be `qd.static` for consistency. The new integer values for `NEIGHBOR_MODE_RADIUS_ONLY`/`K_NEAREST` are also never given. The existing pruning test uses the literal `neighbor_mode != 0` (`:420`), and removing `K_FIRST=0` changes what that literal means.

findings.title: `coherent_to_original` duplicates `sorted_agent_ids`, and `profile_index_c` has no reader
findings.description:
- **`coherent_to_original`:** The reindex sets `_coherent_to_original[kk] = _sorted_agent_ids[kk]` (line 120), so it is the same array, not an inverse permutation. `_sorted_agent_ids[kk]` is already read sequentially in `kk` (`quadrants_fused_kernels.py:437`), so self-exclusion can stay `_sorted_agent_ids[kk] != i` with no new field. Several parts of the design exist only because of this field and can go with it: the "Inverse permutation" decision, Risk 2 (line 425), the permutation assertion in verification step 1 (already covered by `tests/bench/test_quadrants_fused.py:157-199`) and the fail-diagnosis at line 395.
- **`profile_index_c`:** The force kernel reads `_profile_index` only for self (`quadrants_fused_kernels.py:357`), never for a neighbor. So `profile_index_c` has no consumer, and line 63's substitution "for `_profile_index`" refers to a read that doesn't exist.

Cutting both removes 2 of the 7 fields and 2 of the 7 writes per slot from the reindex.

findings.title: Component list omits files the design changes
findings.description:
Line 93 says "No file outside the GPU compute path is touched", but the change also reaches:
- `migratory_server/config.py:311-347` (default, `_VALID_NEIGHBOR_MODES`, error)
- `migratory/bench/workload.py:118,171-175` (its own hard-coded `{"k_first","k_nearest"}` set)
- `migratory_server/gpu_driver.py:24-25,82,110-112`
- `bench/backends/quadrants_fused_backend.py:36-37,93-95`

Both `gpu_driver` and `quadrants_fused_backend` resolve the mode with `_NEIGHBOR_MODE_MAP.get(name, NEIGHBOR_MODE_DEFAULT)`. Once `k_first` leaves the map, any `k_first` string that gets past parsing (see the deprecation-window finding below) silently maps to the default instead of failing. That contradicts line 199's "No silent migration". The design should list these files and replace `.get(..., DEFAULT)` with a lookup that fails.

findings.title: `ConfigurationError` doesn't exist
findings.description:
Lines 67, 199 and 349 say a `ConfigurationError` is raised at parse time. There is no such class anywhere in `src/`. `_parse_compute_config` and `Workload.from_dict` raise `ValueError`, and the bench CLI catches only `(KeyError, ValueError, RuntimeError, FileNotFoundError)` (`cli.py:93`). A new exception that isn't a `ValueError` subclass would surface as an uncaught traceback in the bench, and the server path would also need a check.

Fix: use `ValueError`, or define `ConfigurationError(ValueError)` and say where it lives. No test of the rejection path is specified either.

findings.title: Intermediate states and the gate-fail path are undefined
findings.description:
The design contradicts itself on `k_first`:
- Line 433 keeps `k_first` "still parsed, with a deprecation warning" until the final commit.
- Lines 67 and 199 raise at parse time.
- Step 2 of the development approach (line 442) already removes `k_first` from the kernel.

Commits 2 and 3 therefore ship `ComputeConfig`/`Workload` defaults of `"k_first"` (`config.py:311`, `workload.py:118`) against a kernel and map that no longer have it. Through the `.get(..., DEFAULT)` fallback the live server would run whatever `NEIGHBOR_MODE_DEFAULT` now points to, and nothing defines that value.

If gate 4 fails, the design gives no state to land in: either `k_first` is already gone and the default still says `"k_first"`, or the commits must be reverted. The design needs to define the default and the map contents at each commit, and what ships if the gate fails.

findings.title: Criterion 3's stop condition assumes less work than `radius_only` actually does
findings.description:
Lines 357, 387 and 424 make "`radius_only` at N=10k must beat 213.9 TPS" a slice-stop condition, justified as "strictly less work than scattered reads + early exit". That premise is wrong.

On `mid-flock-10k` (query_radius 50, S=1), `k_first` stops after 32 accepted neighbors. `radius_only` scans and accumulates every candidate: about 1400 per agent, using the design's own figure. That is roughly 40× more inner-loop iterations against a hoped-for 2–3× bandwidth gain. It is also a different physical model on that workload, with no cap and averaging over every candidate.

The check would likely stop the slice for reasons unrelated to reindex cost. A better test of reindex cost is to time the reindex kernel directly, or compare `k_nearest` before and after the change.

findings.title: Parity criterion misstates the existing test and doesn't cover `k_nearest`
findings.description:
Criterion 2 says `tests/bench/test_quadrants_fused_parity.py` checks 5% at N=4500. In the code:
- It loads `mid-flock.yaml` (`:60,175`), which is N=3500 (`bench/workloads/mid-flock.yaml:6`).
- It asserts 20% tolerance (`:116-117,237-238`).
- That YAML sets no `neighbor_mode`, so the test runs the default mode, which is `k_first` until step 4.

As written, "continues to pass" doesn't exercise the coherent `k_nearest` path, and doesn't meet the plan's 5% requirement. The test needs a `k_nearest` variant at 5%, and the design should list it in scope.

findings.title: Verification commands, flags, workloads and config don't exist
findings.description:
Walking the verification steps in order:
- **Steps 2–5:** `cli.py` has no `run` or `parity` subcommand and no `--neighbor-mode` or `--ticks` flag. The only options are `--workload`, `--backend`, `--workload-dir`, `--results-dir` and the `--list-*` flags. `neighbor_mode` is a workload YAML field (`workload.py:171`).
- **Step 5:** needs `mid-flock-500k` and `mid-flock-1M`, but only `mid-flock-200k` is planned (lines 367, 443, 452).
- **Workload sizing:** "Matching mid-flock-10k shape, scaled" doesn't pin the density. `mid-flock-50k.yaml` is actually n=100000.
- **Step 6:** `config/x-fractal.yaml` isn't in the repo (only `default`, `test`, `test-soft-bounds`, `no-populations`, `invalid-population`). The design gives it as N=4500 (line 359) but as ~10000 / 9998 orbs (lines 27, 185).
- **Step 7:** no test in `tests/` mentions `neighbor_mode`, so `pytest -k neighbor_mode` collects nothing (pytest exit code 5).

The commands should be rewritten against the real CLI, the per-mode YAML workloads should be specified, and the tests should be named.

findings.title: Architecture's absolute TPS target isn't restated
findings.description:
The slice is on the GPU tick path that carries the architecture's per-tier TPS NFRs (60 TPS; Tier 3 = 250k, per arch line 74 and plan line 81). The design only gives relative gates (`k_nearest` ≥ 0.8× `radius_only`) and calls Tier 3 "N=200k" (lines 17, 44).

A relative gate can pass while both modes run far below the tier target. The design should restate the Tier 3 target (60 TPS at 250k on production-class hardware) and say what absolute TPS this slice commits to on the dev box.

findings.title: Slice 150 is described as shipped but isn't complete
findings.description: Line 81 says "Slice 150 is shipped on `main` as of 2026-05-05". Slice 150's frontmatter says `status: in_progress`, and the plan shows `[ ] (150)` (plan line 52). Separately, the 213.9 TPS baseline (lines 357, 387, 424) is the slice 149 first-k-found number, per the 150 doc lines 77 and 201. The design should acknowledge that this dependency is still open, or wait until 150 is closed.

findings.title: Overweight narrative and optional measurement scope
findings.description:
Content that could be cut:
- "Reference points" (lines 36-44), parts of "Value" (lines 46-55) and the FRNN rationale (lines 187-193) repeat the 16M-boids comparison three or four times. None of it bears on the gate.
- The 500k/1M headroom probe (lines 397-402) is "not a hard gate" but needs two workloads nothing else uses. Defer it to the FRNN slice it is meant to justify.

findings.title: Wrong claim that spawn/despawn re-runs `setup()`
findings.description: `GpuSimulationDriver.sync_from_entity_manager` (`gpu_driver.py:180-210`) re-uploads into the existing fields; it doesn't call `setup()` or reallocate. The outcome is harmless for coherent fields, which are rebuilt every tick at the same `n`, but the reasoning is wrong.

findings.title: Future Work contradicts the writeback claim
findings.description: Line 461 says "Currently writebacks scatter to `_px[i]`", but line 331 says those writebacks are "sequential in `i`, already coalesced".

findings.title: Placing the reindex in `build_spatial_hash` covers both callers
findings.description: Both `run_fused_tick` (`quadrants_fused_kernels.py:638`) and the production `GpuSimulationDriver.step` (`gpu_driver.py:158`) call `build_spatial_hash` before the force kernel, so one insertion point covers bench and server.

findings.title: Original-order fields stay canonical; memory cost is right
findings.description: `export_positions`, `export_velocities`, `upload_positions` and `sync_from_entity_manager` all work on the original fields, so treating coherent fields as per-tick scratch is safe. 7 × 4 B × 200k = 5.6 MB is correct (5 fields, 4.0 MB, after the cut above). The heap helpers don't care what the payload is (`quadrants_fused_kernels.py:204-301`), as the design says.
